text_in_image: pls go through quoted post to understand key metrics you can check in Qtrly results (few reported annually)
Many aspects to trading results (judging how price will react, collating which firms about to declare results & adding to watchlist & setting alerts, executing the trade)
A- judging how price will react, factors which determine price post results:
1) pre earnings move - if stock has already rallied before results in anticipation, it can fall or be sideways even after superb results
2) YoY (year on year) and QoQ (qtr on Qtr) - absolute & %tage jump in sales, net profit, OPM
3) conference call updates - nowadays this often leads to volatile moves even a day post results if management gives some unexpected guidance or talks about some unknown issues
4) price of the stock (is it near recent lows or recent highs or just about to breakout) - excellent results when price near lows can lead to big bump as it was unexpected
5) are the results a one time/cyclical or do market participants expect the growth to continue for more qtrs
6) market conditions - even good results can see fall in bear markets
7) luck - if broader markets are in free fall that day, most speculators will hesitate to buy intra day even if results are good
8) which stage is the stock in - stage 2 (trending up), stage 4 (decline) or other
9) nature of the stock - does it react violently to results (check past results to evaluate)
10) sector strength & valuation - in a strong theme, okish results can also get lapped up if valuations very low

text_in_image: Natural Gas Transmission: Steady, with Infra Upside
Petrochemicals & Polymer: Structural Pain, Strategic Pivot

JCC index lag created the bonanza: Sales linked to a nine-month JCC average realized very high prices while sourcing costs reflected a lower three-month average, producing an arbitrage that management calls "extraordinary" and "one-off."

Full-year guidance held despite Q1 surge: Management kept the FY27 gas marketing PBT guidance at ~₹4,500 cr, implying the remaining three quarters will contribute only ~₹1,150 cr combined as the index gap closes.

Q2 margin compression flagged explicitly: The nine-month average will begin reflecting current Brent prices, so "the same kind of margins that we earned in quarter one may not be available in quarter two."
Unidentified Speaker: "There has been in earlier years also, cash flow differences have been there... This is one-off, definitely. Much of it will get cured within the year."
